title: Moonglade
body: Moonglade is the sacred valley of the druids, a hidden forest ringed by high mountains between Felwood and Winterspring. The only road in runs through the tunnels of Timbermaw Hold. Druids have revered this place since ancient days: the demigod Cenarius once dwelt here, and here Malfurion Stormrage gathered the first druids into the Cenarion Circle. Its wooded hills hide barrow dens where druids sleep while their spirits walk the Emerald Dream, and in the Third War Tyrande Whisperwind fought her way here to wake Malfurion from his. In the years after Hyjal the glade was opened to druids of every race, tauren as well as night elf, under the guardianship of Keeper Remulos, son of Cenarius. The village of Nighthaven stands beside Lake Elune'ara, and its wardens allow no fighting, so Horde and Alliance meet here as guests of the Circle. Yet the peace has limits: tensions are growing between the druids of Moonglade and the Arch Druid of Darnassus.

title: Nighthaven
body: Nighthaven is the village of Moonglade and the seat of the Cenarion Circle, a quiet cluster of night elf halls and moonwells near the shore of Lake Elune'ara. Its welcome extends to every being who respects the authority and command of nature, on one condition: the balance must be kept, and the Moonglade Wardens are trained to end any hostility without question. Loganaar trains druids here and warns the young that one day the Emerald Dream will call them into a long hibernation. Keeper Remulos' majordomo Rabine Saturna receives visitors, the eccentric archivist Umber keeps the Circle's records, and merchants serve those passing through. Only druids may take the Circle's flights to Thunder Bluff and Rut'theran Village.

title: Lake Elune'ara
body: Lake Elune'ara fills the heart of Moonglade, a broad sheet of clear water bearing the name of the moon goddess, with the village of Nighthaven on its shore and a warden of the Circle keeping watch along its banks. Young druids learning the aquatic form dive into its depths for a shrine bauble that crumbles away quickly, then race with it to the Shrine of Remulos before it fails, sometimes against other students on the same errand.

title: Shrine of Remulos
body: West of Nighthaven stands the Shrine of Remulos, honoring the keeper who guides the Cenarion Circle in preserving nature and its balance. Remulos keeps watch there, and the warden Tajarri expects every visitor to behave as befits sacred ground, at least those who would rather not meet her scimitar. Young druids end their Trial of the Lake here, using the shrine bauble as a nod to the shrine's importance within the Circle, and in the shrine's presence they join the halves of the Pendant of the Sea Lion.

title: Stormrage Barrow Dens
body: The hills of southeastern Moonglade hold the Stormrage Barrow Dens, sacred chambers where night elf druids sleep while their spirits walk the Emerald Dream. Keeper Remulos watches over every druid who hibernates in the glade, and Loganaar, who trains the druids of Nighthaven, warns the young that the call of the Dream will one day take hold of them too, and that they will sleep for many years. The dens are named for Malfurion Stormrage, who slept within them through the ages until the Third War, when Tyrande Whisperwind fought her way into Moonglade to wake him.

title: Keeper Remulos
body: Keeper Remulos, son of the demigod Cenarius, keeps Moonglade, the sacred heart of all druidic study, and his shrine stands west of Nighthaven. He welcomed the tauren into the Circle, and there is open tension between him and Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm. Of late he speaks of the Emerald Dream with grave unease. It has become a dangerous place, he says, and he grows ever more concerned for those who have given up their waking lives in Azeroth in hopes of saving it.

parts.body: A seed carried from Maraudon brought him word of his brother Zaetar, long dead at the hands of the centaur, his own misbegotten children. Remulos had thought him lost to arrogance and anger. Told that Zaetar's spirit lives on there, its remains nourishing new life, he took the seed as proof that his brother had found peace and been reborn into nature, and he senses it will one day matter to this war-torn land.

title: Rabine Saturna
body: Rabine Saturna is Keeper Remulos' majordomo, the night elf who welcomes all who come to aid the Circle on behalf of every denizen of the glade. To Horde volunteers he says that the tauren's devotion to the tenets of Cenarius has earned the Horde a welcome here. To the Alliance, knowing the Arch Druid of Darnassus frowned on their coming, he promises safety from any ill-conceived repercussions, for the work serves the greater good. Umber calls him the den mother of their little bear camp. Behind his courtesy lies a private devotion: the memory of Millicent Serene, Milli as he calls her, the naturalist of Eldre'Thalas whose crowning creation is now being twisted into the Felvine.

title: Dendrite Starblaze
body: Dendrite Starblaze is the night elf druid in Nighthaven to whom the young druids of Darnassus and Thunder Bluff alike are sent. He greets every visitor in the Circle's name and asks that the balance be kept. To the young he is guide and examiner at once: he sends them to the Great Bear Spirit, sets the trials of the lake and the sea lion, and answers cries for help from distant villages by sending students to do real work rather than staged tests. When a new druid first stands before him, he traces an unseen gesture in the air, an aura of power settles over him, and he murmurs to Father Cenarius that it has begun.

title: Umber
body: Umber is the Cenarion Circle's archivist in Nighthaven, a human among the night elves of the glade. He can lay hands on anything the Circle has stored away, provided the asker already knows what they are looking for, an arrangement he finds brilliant. Layo Starstrike in Silithus calls him touched but brilliant, a man who has saved tomes in worse shape than anyone thought could be saved. His manners are his own. He will tell a weary traveler frankly that they smell a bit ripe, and he has no love for anything bug-like, which suits him well enough: the horrors of Silithus can stay out there, and he can stay here with the books.

title: Tajarri
body: Tajarri is a night elf warden of Moonglade, posted at the Shrine of Remulos. Guarding the shrine is her duty and her privilege, she says, and she expects visitors to conduct themselves as guests on sacred ground, at least those who would rather not have her scimitar buried in them. She also has a hand in the teaching of young druids. Students who race up from Lake Elune'ara with a crumbling shrine bauble report to her to finish the Trial of the Lake, and she congratulates each one warmly before setting the Trial of the Sea Lion and sending them to ask the people of the glade where the two halves of the pendant may lie.

title: Great Bear Spirit
body: In the northwest of Moonglade dwells the Great Bear Spirit, a wise and noble being the druids say has been part of Azeroth for as long as Azeroth has existed. It speaks without moving its mouth, its voice simply heard, and every druid of the Claw comes to it at the start of the path. It represents the strength that bolsters a young druid, and teaches two lessons. Strength of body is power and swiftness, the bear's great girth hiding a lithe agility and a sharp mind. Strength of heart is the resolve to act from pure intent, the conviction of a mother bear guarding her young. Keeping the balance, it warns, is never mere complacency.

title: Bunthen Plainswind and Silva Fil'naveth
body: Two flight masters stand together in Nighthaven, and they serve druids alone. Silva Fil'naveth, a night elf, offers the Cenarion Circle's flight to Rut'theran Village below Darnassus, while her tauren counterpart Bunthen Plainswind carries druids to Thunder Bluff, and each sends the other's people to their partner. In that small courtesy lies the glade's whole purpose: night elf and tauren side by side in the Circle's service. Anyone else who asks for a ride is told plainly that they are not a druid. Other travelers must make do with the hippogryph master Sindrayl and the wind rider master Faustron, who keep their own posts out in the open glade beyond the village.

title: The Way of the Claw
body: When a young druid is ready to learn the shape of the bear, the trainer, Mathrengyl Bearwalker in Darnassus or Turak Runetotem in Thunder Bluff, teaches the spell that carries druids to Moonglade and sends the student to Dendrite Starblaze. The night elf is reminded that all druids are welcome there, whatever the tensions between the Arch Druid and Keeper Remulos; the tauren is told that Remulos watches over every druid who sleeps in the glade. Dendrite greets the student with a quiet word to Father Cenarius that it has begun, and sets them on the path of the bear: first they must seek out the Great Bear Spirit in the northwest of the glade, mentor to every druid, and learn what it will teach.

parts.body: The Great Bear Spirit teaches strength of body and strength of heart, and sends the student away with its blessing and a warning that their strength will one day be tested. Dendrite senses a new wisdom in them, a strength and knowing intent not yet focused, and sends them home to the trainer who sent them.

parts.body: Back in Darnassus, Mathrengyl explains that the Great Bear Spirit has been part of Azeroth for as long as Azeroth has existed, and that druids rely on its wisdom and power. Then he sets the last test. In the moonkin cave nearest Auberdine stands a Moonkin Stone, and its defender Lunaclaw comes forth only when Cenarion moondust is laid upon it. Its strength must be faced before the way of the Claw is learned.

title: The Trials of the Lake and the Sea Lion
body: The aquatic form is a blessing that must be earned. Druids who have grown into worthy protectors of nature are sent from Darnassus and Thunder Bluff to Dendrite Starblaze, who sets them two trials. The first tests work in water under pressure: the student dives into Lake Elune'ara for a shrine bauble, which decays rapidly, and must carry it to the Shrine of Remulos before it fails, perhaps racing other druids on the same errand, then use it there and report to the warden Tajarri, one of Moonglade's most trusted.

parts.body: Using the bauble at the shrine honors its importance within the Circle, and Tajarri congratulates each student who succeeds. Then she sets the second trial, which tests understanding of the form itself. The Pendant of the Sea Lion must be made whole from two halves, one holding the sea lion's agility in the water, the other its endurance, and the people of the glade hold the clues to where they lie.

title: Lessons Anew
body: Druids can purge poison with a single incantation, a gift of Cenarius not to be taken lightly. Before they learn it, the trainers of Darnassus and Thunder Bluff send their students to Dendrite Starblaze to learn what poison means for those without that power. There are no staged trials here, for real calls for help have reached Moonglade. In Auberdine, Alanndarian Nightsong cannot stop a sickness among the deer of Darkshore, and Dendrite suspects the Cliffspring Falls, the region's main source of drinking water. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem faces the same among the gazelles of the northern Barrens, and the suspicion falls on the pools atop Dreadmist Peak, where the Burning Blade dwell.

parts.body: Alanndarian finds the water from Cliffspring Falls disgusting. Something is fouling Darkshore's whole water table, and sick deer are seen far from the river, yet she senses that something else is at work as well. The tainted water itself will be the base of her curative salve, with earthroot for healing and, for potency, lunar fungus from the caves to the east, where the moonkin have grown irritable.

The student, like the elders of Thunder Bluff, has shown that the need for balance transcends artificial racial barriers, and has proven a friend of nature and the Circle.

title: The Fruit of Fertility
body: Agents of the Cenarion Circle have brought Rabine Saturna troubling news from Eldre'Thalas, the ruin now called Dire Maul. Long ago a night elf naturalist there, Millicent Serene, willed the power of nature into artifacts, and her crowning work was the Fruit of Fertility, a vibrant vine grown from a specially prepared moonwell whose aura of protection and growth made all of Eldre'Thalas flourish. The Circle believed it destroyed in the War of the Ancients. It survived, and the demon Alzzin the Wildshaper is corrupting it into the Felvine. Rabine will not let that corruption run its course, for the world's sake and for Milli's memory. So vile a thing can only be held in a Reliquary of Purity, and he knows one lay in the ruins of Southwind Village in Silithus many years ago.

With turmoil rising in Silithus he had kept it secret, since prying would only rouse the suspicions of the Circle's enemies. Now he asks for the rest: to face Alzzin in the east of Dire Maul and, when the demon falls, seal a shard of the Felvine inside.

parts.body: The sealed reliquary reaches Nighthaven. With it the Circle can remove a corrupting threat from the world and study it under its own watch, perhaps finding new means against the taint, and Rabine knows Milli would have had it no other way. The war is far from over, he says, but a great battle has been won, and its bearer is welcomed as a hero of the Cenarion Circle.

title: The Redemption of Eranikus
body: The champion who seeks the green shard of the Scepter of the Shifting Sands must recover it from Eranikus, a dragon of Ysera's flight. In the Sunken Temple, Malfurion warned that the power of the Old Gods had twisted him into a tyrant of the Dream who would never give the shard up freely, and that there was only one way: bring Eranikus into the world. A wisp outside Darnassus carried word to Tyrande and sent the champion on to Keeper Remulos. Eranikus could never be pulled from the Dream against his will, Remulos explains, but he wishes to come, for he means to destroy Malfurion's sleeping body, and with it one of the Dream's mightiest allies. First, fragments of the Nightmare's corruption must be taken from the dragonkin at the four dream portals.

Through the fragments he finds the Nightmare's origin and opens the rift above Lake Elune'ara, well away from Malfurion. Eranikus is to be redeemed, not destroyed: his blows must be weathered and Nighthaven saved until Tyrande arrives.

title: Shrouded in Nightmare
body: Four dragons of Ysera's flight have come forth from the dream portals of Duskwood, the Hinterlands, Ashenvale and Feralas, corrupted and sick with nightmare: Taerar, Lethon, Ysondre and Emeriss. Those who bring one down find an object engulfed in nightmares, corruption seeping from it, that seems to tie the dragons to the Dream itself. It cannot be read by just anyone. Only a druid of great power could decipher its meaning, perhaps one of the druids of Moonglade, or of Cenarion Hold in the south.

parts.body: As the taint washed away, Malfurion Stormrage appeared to his old friend, the message having found its way to him. A new foe fought them in the Dream, Malfurion said, born of an ancient evil: Ysera's noble brood had fallen to the old whisperings, and the Nightmare sought a new host on Azeroth. Cenarius fought at his side, he said, and Illidan brooded on his throne in Outland, sunk in madness. Then Malfurion was drawn back, asking Remulos to tell Tyrande he was safe and would return. His signet ring went to the messenger.

title: The Journal Under the Chitin
body: Rabine Saturna's call to Horde and Alliance alike leads beyond Tanaris and Un'Goro, to the wasteland of Silithus. Few know, he says, that the night elves once fought a malign and alien power there; it was sealed away, but the Circle suspects that something now works to stir it. He sends volunteers with a letter to Layo Starstrike, one of the Circle's agents, at Valor's Rest, the resting place of those who fell in the wastes, and promises that Layo's trust will follow the letter.

Umber the archivist promises to crack its shell and share what he finds, and sends the bearer on to the den mother of their little bear camp, Rabine, who must never be kept waiting unless one cares to be doused in honey.
